scope: One standalone native GtkButton; painting ACTIVE versus physical held input. No product capability enabled.
findings: Default displacement0 masks the difference; both child allocations coincide
With displacement2 native child moves45,45 to47,47; forced ACTIVE leaves45,45
Both have GtkState ACTIVE and outer180x60; state/outer dimensions alone do not prove pressed equivalence
Forced display emitted no activation; restored physical press/release activated exactly once
limitations: Uses private geometry-only RC, not generated DomainOS recipe paint proof
No Motif/VM fidelity, mouse-hover persistence, rebuild or scene integration proof
Failed initial Gdk.get_origin binding call was fixed by private X11 window coordinates; prior failure log retained
Bridge proof is only standalone normal/forced/reset/physical press; hover, scene rebuild, painting equivalence and other button subclasses remain unproved.
next: Design the scoped GTK2 bridge lifecycle/capability before scene integration, then prove rebuild and coupled/separate paths; exact-runtime ABI guard and native paint comparison remain required.

native_signal_hypothesis.result: enter/pressed/leave/released alone did not produce ACTIVE or native child displacement; rejected as implementation shortcut. Diagnostics retained before assertion.

native_crossing.result: Local crossing events plus press reproduce native child displacement; input flags change, so not promoted to product.

visual_bridge.risk: Uses exposed GTK2 struct field depressed, exact compile/runtime version guarded. This is not a portable public setter; GTK3 and other GTK2 versions unsupported by this experiment.

hover_lifecycle.finding: Native crossing updates remove visual depressed state unless reapplied after native handlers.
hover_lifecycle.callbacks_scope: Only the standalone private GtkButton; disconnected before restoring native interaction.
